text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 8.1% today, extending a two-week decline to 16%. The stock dropped sharply after the company released its quarterly earnings and financial report on November 3rd—the timing of the earnings announcement coinciding with the stock's turn lower. Oil refiners like Marathon are sensitive to the spread between crude oil input costs and refined product prices; with US oil at $99.64 per barrel and refineries running at 94.5% capacity, the margin environment appears constrained, and whatever guidance the company provided in earnings evidently disappointed the market.

Broader headwinds are also weighing on the sector. The gap between US crude ($99.64) and world crude ($107.03) suggests tightening margins for US refiners, and market commentary ahead of earnings warned that investor caution could emerge even if earnings themselves are strong—suggesting the market may be repositioning away from big energy as the political landscape shifts and the focus moves toward longer-term demand uncertainty.
